items.title: Devils coach Keefe says sitting Hellebuyck vs. Jets was GM Mehta’s decision
items.summary: Mehta stated that a “reduction in win probability” was the reason behind not play Hellebuyck against his former team.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect While there’s still confusion about why New Jersey Devils goaltender Connor Hellebuyck is not being allowed to play against his former team, at least we’re getting some clarification on who made the call. When speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Devils head coach Sheldon Keefe revealed that he had little to do with the decision to withhold Hellebuyck from starting against the Winnipeg Jets, stating that the decision came from the top – general manager Sunny Mehta. “The competitor in me, of course, wants to get Connor out there,” Keefe said. “Let’s go, let’s get at it. But Sunny made the decision he didn’t want him to be a part of this.” The Devils were fiercely criticized when Mehta put out a statement late Sunday night, confirming that Hellebuyck wouldn’t play in Winnipeg, the first time New Jersey is playing in Manitoba since the blockbuster trade that saw the Devils send forwards Nick Bjugstad, Dawson Mercer and Alexander Command, goaltender Nico Daws, a second-round pick in the 2029 NHL Draft, and a seventh-rounder in 2027 to Winnipeg. “This has been an organizational decision for us that we’ve debated at length,” Mehta said. “Connor Hellebuyck was adamant that he felt a duty to play on Tuesday in Winnipeg. However, in our estimation, playing in this game would potentially give us a reduction in our expected win probability.” Mehta added that Hellebuyck is going to speak to the media prior to Tuesday’s clash, per his request. In each of his first five starts with his new team, the Commerce, Mich. native has been victorious, posting a 1.96 goals-against average, a .913 save percentage and a shutout. items.title: Red Wings activate Marco Kasper, Mason Appleton off IR
items.summary: Kasper has missed all but one game this season, while Appleton has missed all but two games.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Danny Wild-Imagn Images The Detroit Red Wings are welcoming a couple of forwards back into their lineup. On Tuesday, the Red Wings announced that they have activated center Marco Kasper and winger Mason Appleton off of injured reserve. Kasper, 22, has been out since Detroit’s season-opening 2-0 loss to the New York Rangers with an upper-body injury. Last season, the Austrian national notched nine goals and 10 assists for 19 points in 81 games. Selected eighth overall by the Red Wings in the 2022 NHL Entry Draft, Kasper spent the 2022-23 season playing mostly for Rögle BK of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL), where he had eight goals and 15 assists for 23 points in 52 games. He also made his NHL debut that season, going scoreless in one game for Detroit. Kasper came to North America full-time for the 2023-24 season, in which he registered 14 goals and 21 assists for 35 points in 71 games for the Red Wings’ American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate Grand Rapids Griffins. His rookie NHL season came in 2024-25, when he put up 19 goals and 18 assists for a career-best 37 points in 77 games. Appleton, 30, went scoreless over Detroit’s first two games this season, but has been out since with an undisclosed injury. Last season, the Green Bay, Wisconsin native had six goals and eight assists for 14 points in 65 games for the Red Wings. Selected by the Winnipeg Jets in the sixth round of the 2015 NHL Draft, Appleton spent seven of his first eight NHL seasons with the Jets, playing just one season for the Seattle Kraken in 2021-22, before signing a two-year, $5.8 million contract with Detroit in July of 2025. His career-best campaign came in 2023-24 with Winnipeg, when he notched 14 goals and 22 assists for 36 points in 82 games.

items.title: The story behind Jake Middleton’s tribute to his grandfather’s wartime sacrifice
items.summary: Jake Middleton wears his family history on his left arm, quite literally. The Flames defenceman’s grandfather served in the Second World War, and Middleton shares his love with a deeply meaningful tattoo sleeve.
items.body: CALGARY — The poppy fell from his father's chest and into the grave. Jake Middleton was seven years old, standing among family and friends near the military base in Wainwright, Alta., watching as they lowered his grandfather, Robert Bruce, into the ground. Somewhere in the emotion of that moment, it came loose and tumbled onto the coffin below. One by one, those gathered for “Papa's” funeral removed their own poppies, stepped forward and tossed them into the grave, sending their final tribute down with the man they had come to say goodbye to. And every Nov. 11, when the trumpets begin to sound, that little boy comes rushing back. "You know, I always get a frog in my throat when those start playing on Remembrance Day," said the Calgary Flames defenceman. It's a memory that has never really left him. Neither has the man who inspired it. Middleton wears his family history on his left arm, quite literally. His extensive tattoo sleeve is a deeply personal tribute to his grandfather, a Second World War dispatch rider who served in North Africa, France, Germany and England. It's a remarkable piece of work, and Middleton has never been particularly shy about showing it off. Those familiar with his entertaining media availabilities know they’re often delivered shirtless. But there's considerably more to it than ink and impressive artwork. There's a grandson's love for a grandfather he lost too young, a family's military history and an appreciation for sacrifices that become increasingly meaningful with age. He remembers his grandfather playing the harmonica, painting houses and spending time in his wood shop. items.body: Register Login Injured Reserve Notes: Kasper, Appleton, Spurgeon By Marcus Antonelli | at November 10, 2026 11:52 am The Detroit Red Wings have activated forwards Marco Kasper and Mason Appleton from injured reserve, the team announced . Two insertions into the lineup that Detroit will welcome with open arms, as they will face St. Louis tonight. Kasper, because of an upper-body injury, has been out for some time. The injury stemmed from Kasper’s second-period fight against New York Rangers defenseman Sean Durzi . Kasper went scoreless in the Red Wings’ season opener, but he earned an impressive 71.4% success rate in the faceoff dot. He enters the final season of a three-year, entry-level contract coming off of a down year from his first full NHL season, 19 points in 2025-26 well off his 37 points in 2024-25. The 30-year-old Appleton is in year two of a contract paying him $2.9MM annually. He has filled a bottom-six role in his first year with the Detroit Red Wings, having scored 14 points in 68 games last season. That depth, grinder role was also seen across the last four seasons with the Winnipeg Jets. He typically held close to 20 points a season, but grew to 14 goals and 36 points in a career year during the 2023-24 season. Even with that rise, Appleton’s biggest impacts tend to come away from the puck and down the lineup, as Detroit has benefited from his penalty-kill ice-time, racking up 84:53 of shorthanded TOI, fifth-most on the Wings since 2025-26 and never allowing a shorthanded goal.

items.title: Will Flyers ‘take an axe’ to veteran core if season doesn’t turn around?
items.summary: A potential lost season could serve as an opportunity to right the ship for the future.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images There isn’t a lot that has gone right for the Philadelphia Flyers this season. They sit with a record of 5-10-5 (despite Monday night’s win versus the Vancouver Canucks ), and a lot of questions are being justifiably asked about the Flyers’ direction and if their current trajectory is a winning one. This is year four of the team being overseen by president of hockey operations Keith Jones and general manager Daniel Briere. Coming off a playoff berth and subsequent first-round series win, expectations were raised for the Flyers by pundits and fans. That being said, Briere himself did make mention of a potential “step back” last summer – it was a hot topic – indicating that the internal expectations were much lower than those of the public. But it would be fair to say that nobody was expecting this much of a regression. Any way you cut it, the Flyers are not going to take the next step without a top-six center – full stop. The front office knows this, as their $90-million offer sheet to Anaheim Ducks center Leo Carlsson was indicative of that. The Flyers have been heavily critiqued for not completely tanking and putting themselves in a position to draft a Carlsson, Connor Bedard or Macklin Celebrini themselves. It is a valid argument, as top-end centers are rarely moved in today’s NHL, and the top of the draft is the most likely place to get them – but it isn’t a guaranteed formula. Yes, the Chicago Blackhawks and San Jose Sharks landed Bedard and Celebrini, respectively, via the draft, but their respective rebuilds aren’t exactly peaches and cream right now. items.title: Maple Leafs’ Tanev says he wants to play more
items.body: One Toronto Maple Leafs veteran feels he doesn't need to be held off the ice. Chris Tanev , who has been limited to nine games this season, isn't happy with the load-management route the Maple Leafs have taken with him. The Toronto native added that while he respects general manager John Chayka and understands the desire to keep him available longer term, they have a difference in opinion on his utilization. Tanev, 36, missed all but 11 games last season after sustaining a serious concussion This season, he suffered an injury on Oct. 10 against the Colorado Avalanche and then missed nine games. Head coach Jim Hiller said that while he wished he could have Tanev in the lineup each night, "there's a plan in place to protect the player and the team." "We've got an unbelievable staff," Hiller added . "They're all working together to make the best decisions for the player and the team." Tanev, perhaps the Maple Leafs' strongest defensive defenceman, has one assist and has averaged 17:46 per game.

items.title: Lightning recall 2025-26 OHL MVP Sam O’Reilly
items.body: A player with a very impressive junior-hockey resume is on the verge of getting his first NHL shot. Sam O'Reilly has been recalled by the Tampa Bay Lightning , the club announced Tuesday. O'Reilly was MVP of the OHL regular season and playoffs as well as the Memorial Cup last season after leading the Kitchener Rangers to the CHL and OHL titles. He was acquired by the Rangers in a mid-season deal with the London Knights, with whom he also won a Memorial Cup and two OHL championships. O'Reilly, 20, also had eight points in seven games for bronze medal-winning Canada at last year's world junior championship. The Toronto native has two goals and four assists in 12 games with AHL Syracuse. The Lightning acquired O'Reilly in a deal with the Edmonton Oilers for Isaac Howard in July 2025. O'Reilly was selected in the first round (32nd overall) by Edmonton in the 2024 NHL Draft. The Lightning are in Buffalo on Wednesday to face the Sabres.

items.title: Wild could keep unsigned Quinn Hughes past trade deadline, GM says
items.body: The Minnesota Wild are going all-in on their Stanley Cup aspirations this season, even if it means losing their star defenceman to free agency. General manager Bill Guerin said Tuesday that the team might opt to keep Quinn Hughes past the trade deadline even if he does not re-sign with the Wild, running the risk of losing the one-time Norris Trophy winner for nothing. “Honestly, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes, so I mean, I want to keep him as long as I possibly can,” Guerin told reporters in Toronto, per NHL.com . “Whether it’s three months, three years, seven years, whatever, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes.” When asked if that would extend to keeping an unsigned Hughes past the trade deadline, Guerin said yes. Hughes, in the final year of a six-year, $47.1-million contract, became eligible to re-sign with the Wild on July 1. On that front, Guerin said progress towards a deal remains "status quo." "Honestly, I just want him to focus on hockey,” Guerin said. “Like I said, he knows what’s going on in his head. He understands everything.” The Wild acquired Hughes from the Vancouver Canucks in December 2025 in exchange for Zeev Buium, Liam Ohgren, Marco Rossi and a 2026 first-round pick.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Bob Frid-Imagn Images It’s official: a former NHL sniper is heading overseas. On Tuesday, the Kontinental Hockey League announced that former NHL winger Evander Kane has signed a one-year contract with HC Sibir Novosibirsk. Kane signs with Sibir, even though multiple reports stated that he was receiving offers from teams on this side of the Atlantic. His agent, Dan Milstein, stated that Kane would be heading to the KHL during last week’s episode of DFO Rundown . The 35-year-old moves to Russia after spending the 2025-26 season with the Vancouver Canucks . On a team that finished with the worst record in the NHL, Kane managed to score 13 goals and 18 assists for 31 points, finishing sixth on the team in scoring, while appearing in 71 games. It came after a rather successful four seasons with the Edmonton Oilers , where Kane’s physical play and scoring touch helped his team reach the Western Conference Finals three times, advancing to the Stanley Cup Final in 2024 and 2025. In 1,001 regular-season games, which included stops with the Buffalo Sabres , San Jose Sharks and Winnipeg Jets (formerly the Atlanta Thrashers), Kane potted 339 goals and 309 assists for 648 pints, with another 55 points in 97 postseason contests. This won’t be the first time Kane has played in Russia. During the lockout that canceled half of the 2012-13 season, he signed with Dynamo Minsk, scoring two points in 12 games. Sibir is 8-1-4-13 so far this season, sitting with the worst record in the KHL’s Eastern Conference and 20th in the league’s overall standings. While it’s not clear when Kane will make his debut, Novosibirsk is in action on Sunday, taking on Dynamo Moscow.

items.body: Register Login Evander Kane Signs With KHL’s Sibir Novosibirsk By Brennan McClain | at November 10, 2026 7:45 am The former fourth-overall pick of the 2009 NHL Draft is taking his talents overseas. According to the KHL , Evander Kane has signed a one-year contract with Sibir Novosibirsk in the KHL. Earlier in November, in speaking to David Pagnotta on DFO Insider , Dan Milstein of Gold Star Hockey confirmed that Evander Kane would sign with a KHL organization and that a formal announcement should be expected in the next few days; the team has officially come to light. Because of his age and poor play during last season with the Vancouver Canucks, Milstein’s announcement strongly suggests that Kane won’t return to the NHL. Although there were plenty of ups and downs, few players get to enjoy a 16-year career like Kane did. That career began on June 26, 2009, when the Atlanta Thrashers selected Kane with the fourth overall pick in the 2009 NHL Draft. He immediately jumped to the NHL, scoring 14 goals and 26 points in 66 games, good for a ninth-place finish in Calder Trophy voting. Kane spent one more season with the Thrashers and remained with the team when they relocated, becoming the second iteration of the Winnipeg Jets. His first season in Winnipeg is arguably his career-best campaign. The Vancouver, BC, native finished second on the team in scoring behind Blake Wheeler , registering 30 goals and 57 points in 74 games with a +11 rating. A few weeks before the 2012-13 campaign was supposed to start, the Jets signed Kane to a six-year, $31.5MM ($5.25MM AAV) extension. Unfortunately, Kane’s relationship with the Jets rapidly began to sour. Toward the end of the 2013-14 campaign, Kane was accused of assault in his hometown and was subsequently sued for financial damages.

items.body: SAN JOSE, Calif. — Ivar Stenberg scored the only goal in a shootout that lasted eight rounds, and the San Jose Sharks beat the New York Islanders 3-2 on Monday night to snap a five-game losing streak. Tyler Toffoli had a goal and an assist, and Stenberg also scored in regulation for the Sharks (8-11-1). Stenberg has six goals and is tied for the scoring lead among NHL rookies. Ben Hutton and Victor Eklund scored for the Islanders (7-6-4), who have lost four straight games (0-2-2). Ilya Sorokin stopped 37 shots. Stenberg put the Sharks on the board late in the first period after Toffoli sent a shot toward the net. Stenberg got a piece of the puck to redirect it past Sorokin and tie the game at 1. San Jose again rallied from a goal down midway through the second when Toffoli’s shot deflected off Islanders defenseman Adam Pelech and into the net. It was Toffoli’s first goal in eight games. Hutton opened the scoring early in the first after Simon Holmstrom’s pass found him with an open look. Eklund put New York ahead 2-1 early in the second with a power-play goal. Sharks center Alexander Wennberg, who returned after missing 10 games, was called for the penalty that led to the power play. The game got chippy late in the second as fights broke out, leading to four five-minute major penalties. Barclay Goodrow received a penalty for fighting Mitchell Chaffee, and Ty Dellandrea was penalized for fighting Kyle MacLean.

items.title: McDavid’s historic assist streak ends in Oilers’ win over Rangers
items.body: For a second on Monday, it appeared that Connor McDavid had extended his historic assist streak to 19 games right at the buzzer in the Edmonton Oilers ' 3-1 win over the New York Rangers. But after a quick ruling from the NHL, McDavid had his helper on Leon Draisaitl's empty-net goal pulled off the scoresheet. As the Rangers pressed on the power play with their net empty in the final two minutes, a rebound came out to McDavid in front of the Oilers' net. Edmonton's captain bumped into New York forward JT Miller in the battle for the puck, which was eventually tipped out to Draisaitl closer to the blue line, where No. 29 flipped it down the ice and into the open cage. Upon closer inspection, Miller's stick was the last to touch the puck before Draisaitl put the game away — bringing McDavid's streak to an end at 18. With assists in 18 straight games, McDavid tied Adam Oates for the second-longest streak in NHL history, behind only Wayne Gretzky’s 23 games set in 1990-91. He did continue his point streak to open the season, however, opening the scoring with his 11th goal in Edmonton's first 19 games — giving him 48 points on the year.

items.summary: If there is one thread that ties the Hockey Hall of Fame’s Class of 2026, it might be the sheer improbability of their paths to the hallowed Hall.
items.body: TORONTO — If there is one thread that ties the Hockey Hall of Fame’s Class of 2026, it might be the sheer improbability of their paths to the hallowed Hall. Of course, breathing the rarefied air fewer than four percent of the game’s all-time roster has shared is reserved for only a select few, but this class faced some of the longest odds before their inductions on Monday night in downtown Toronto. Generational goaltender Carey Price hailed from Ulkatcho First Nation in Anahim Lake, B.C. “Growing up in a remote community, there was a very slim chance of this happening without a relentless desire and opportunity,” Price said in his induction speech on Monday. Life is funny.” Patrice Bergeron burst onto the scene as an 18-year-old rookie but the player the Boston Bruins chose over Joe Thornton to build around also faced a career crossroads in his 20s when he missed nearly an entire season with multiple concussions. items.title: Keith Tkachuk celebrates his children during emotional Hall of Fame speech
items.summary: The former NHLer said being a father was ‘the greatest title’ he ever had as he was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-US PRESSWIRE Keith Tkachuk celebrated his three children and the rest of his family as the former NHLer gave his Hockey Hall of Fame induction speech in Toronto Monday night. “To my children, Matthew, Brady and Taryn: Being your father is the greatest title I’ve ever had,” Keith Tkachuk said. “Taryn, you are a smart, strong, beautiful, quick witted, and may have the most hockey knowledge in the family. Brady, you’re the most caring and thoughtful person I know. Matthew, you made me a father for the first time and filled me with joy. I didn’t know it was possible.” The father said watching his two sons play with the U.S. Olympic men’s hockey team, and now with the Florida Panthers , “has been the thrill of a lifetime.” Keith Tkachuk was inducted as part of the 2026 Hall of Fame class, along with Carey Price, Patrice Bergeron, Cindy Curley, Pekka Rinne and Brian Burke. “This game has welcomed me at every level. I accept this honour with gratitude to everyone who has been part of my journey,” Keith Tkachuk said. It’s been a busy week for Keith Tkachuk. Last Saturday in Toronto, the 54-year-old retired winger was booed as we was introduced with his fellow inductees before the Toronto Maple Leafs hosted the New Jersey Devils in the annual Hockey Hall of Fame Game. Keith Tkachuk had 538 goals and 527 assists for 1,065 points and 2,219 penalty minutes in 1,201 regular-season games with the Winnipeg Jets , Phoenix Coyotes , St. Louis Blues and Atlanta Thrashers. "It's pretty special to be able to look around," Price said before adding with a smile: "I was hoping to get the chance to shoot on myself downstairs." The 39-year-old was once at the pinnacle of his craft. Now he's taken his place alongside the game's greats. Price was inducted into the Hall as part of the 2026 class alongside Patrice Bergeron, Pekka Rinne, Keith Tkachuk and Cindy Curley in the player category Monday. The No. 5 pick at the 2005 draft, Price won the Hart Trophy as league MVP and the Vezina Trophy as its top goaltender in 2015. items.body: Register Login Capitals Recall Justin Holl By Brennan McClain | at November 9, 2026 5:00 pm The Washington Capitals had a roster spot to fill after losing netminder Rémi Poirier off waivers earlier this afternoon. Washington quickly filled it, announcing they recalled defenseman Justin Holl from the AHL’s Hershey Bears. Holl, 34, earns his second call-up of the 2026-27 season. The Capitals signed Holl to a one-year, $900K contract this past offseason and recalled him earlier this season after Washington’s defensive corps suffered a few injuries. He looked good in his debut with Washington, scoring two goals in three games with a +1 rating, while averaging 12:59 of ice time per game. It’s a solid change of pace for Holl after the 10-year blueliner suffered through the worst stretch of his professional career with the Detroit Red Wings. Ahead of the 2023-24 season, the Red Wings signed Holl to a three-year, $10.2MM ($3.4MM AAV) contract after he spent the previous six years with the Toronto Maple Leafs. It started poorly, as Holl finished with only five assists in 38 games in his first season. Holl struggled again during the 2024-25 season, prompting Detroit to demote him. Last campaign, the final season of his three-year pact, Holl played exclusively for the Grand Rapids Griffins in the AHL before he was traded to the St. Louis Blues as a salary offset for the Justin Faulk trade. In fairness to Holl, he was never known as an offensive threat, but his production in Detroit was far lower than he was accustomed to in Toronto. Still, he also began to struggle defensively, producing a career-worst takeaway-to-turnover ratio in the 2024-25 season. Regardless, he has appeared far more comfortable in his limited action with the Capitals.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The hockey world has lost a member of the Montreal Canadiens ‘ 1971 Stanley Cup championship team. On Monday, the NHL Alumni Association announced that former center Bobby Sheehan passed away at the age of 77. The Weymouth, Massachusetts native was selected by the Canadiens out of the Ontario Hockey Association’s St. Catherines Black Hawks in the 1969 NHL Amateur Draft. He spent his first two professional seasons in Montreal’s organization, playing 45 total regular season games with the Canadiens and winning the Stanley Cup with Montreal in 1971. Sheehan joined the California Golden Seals for the 1971-72 season, where he scored 20 goals and added 26 assists for 46 points in 78 games. Following his lone season with the Golden Seals, Sheehan had a three-year stint in the World Hockey Association (WHA). His 1972-73 season with the WHA’s New York Raiders was the best of his career, putting up 35 goals and 53 assists for 88 points in 75 games. He stayed with New York (which would be renamed the New York Golden Blades and then the Jersey Knights) for most of the 1973-74 season before moving on to the Edmonton Oilers through the 1974-75 season. Sheehan returned to the NHL with the Chicago Black Hawks in the 1975-76 season, and then played for the Detroit Red Wings in the 1976-77 season. He went back to the WHA for one last season in 1977-78, when played for the Indianapolis Racers. Sheehan then spent the rest of his career splitting time between the New York Rangers , Colorado Rockies, and Los Angeles Kings of the NHL, the New Haven Nighthawks and Binghamton Whalers of the American Hockey League (AHL), and the Forth Worth Texans of the Central Hockey League (CHL), before retiring in 1983. items.title: Spotlight on Flames defenceman Nemec after Bahl injury
items.summary: After the Flames lost Kevin Bahl to injury, the interesting part became who would step up. His partner, Simon Nemec, now has an opportunity, writes Eric Francis.
items.body: CALGARY - The Calgary Flames have lost their best defenceman, their most reliable matchup player and, according to head coach Ryan Huska, their best player through the opening portion of the season. Kevin Bahl’s season-ending Achilles injury is a harsh blow to a rebuilding team trying to remain competitive and establish some consistency in a season that figures to have its share of growing pains. The Flames immediately addressed the loss of the six-foot-six lefty by replacing him on the top pairing the last two games with 35-year-old Joel Hanley. But the spotlight is now squarely on his partner, Simon Nemec . We're about to find out a whole lot more about the 22-year-old former second overall pick who arrived in Calgary this summer for two first round picks and a second. The price tag suggests he’ll be one of the organization's foundational pieces. Now we’ll pay even more attention to how he’s progressing towards that status. He’s been thrust into an even more pressure-packed situation — the kind he insisted he wanted so badly in Jersey. He insists there was already plenty of pressure, given the five-year, $36 million deal he signed this summer. But he won't be able to lean on Bahl like he has so far. “I feel like we were probably the perfect pair, if you see the size, the hands, and the style of hockey, so that is probably is gonna change a little bit,” said Nemec. “He's the reason why my game has been growing up, but I don't want to say it was just because of him. Poirier, 25, now returns to the organization that drafted him and with which he began this season before a series of transactions. The Stars waived him at the end of training camp and the preseason with the intent to assign him to their AHL affiliate Texas Stars, but he was claimed by the New Jersey Devils, who had considerable organizational need for goaltending depth at the time. Now, he returns to the Stars, who chose him with the No. 185 overall selection in the sixth round of the 2020 draft. The Quebec native turned pro after wrapping up his major junior career with the Gatineau Olympiques of the QMJHL in 2021-22. Poirier has yet to appear in a game at the NHL or AHL level this season. items.title: Arniel criticizes Devils’ decision not to play Hellebuyck vs. Jets: Goalie ‘gave up on us’
items.summary: The Winnipeg Jets aren’t too happy with the New Jersey Devils’ decision to bench Connor Hellebuyck in his return to Manitoba.
items.body: The Winnipeg Jets aren't too happy with the New Jersey Devils ' decision to bench Connor Hellebuyck in his return to Manitoba. Head coach Scott Arniel bashed the decision on Monday, citing a lack of closure for fans and teammates. "We've seen some other players go back to their buildings and do it and get it over and done with," Arniel said. "I know it's their decision and they can do whatever they want, but I think that it would put closure (to the situation). This doesn't. We're gonna see them in (nine) games in their building and I'm sure he's going to be in the net then. "To me, it goes back to the ownership, it goes back to the fans, it goes back to the core guys that have been with Helle from the very beginning that he kind of left on. ... He just gave up on us. It would be nice to finally be done with this," Arniel added. "I can feel the frustration of the fans. We wanted to get this put to bed. That’s the biggest thing. Now it’s not getting put to bed here. It’s going to linger again." The Devils announced on Sunday night that Hellebuyck would not play against his former team, with general manager Sunny Mehta citing a "reduction in our expected win probability" as the reasoning. “I’m disappointed, but I understand. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Some unwanted news for a team already experiencing enough struggles this season. When speaking to the media, Columbus Blue Jackets head coach Rick Bowness announced that forward Conor Garland will not be in the lineup on Tuesday night, when the Blue Jackets take on the Florida Panthers . Bowness said Garland is battling back from an upper-body injury but didn’t provide a timeline for his return. It isn’t quite clear when or where Garland was hurt. He played the entirety of Columbus’ last contest, a 5-2 loss to the Buffalo Sabres this past Friday night. The 30-year-old was a -2 while logging a little over 13 minutes of ice time, not too far from his average for the year. Garland had appeared in each of the Jackets’ first 15 games of the 2026-27 season, but has definitely looked far from the offensive threat he was earlier in his career. He has just one assist to his name to go along with his plus/minus of -5 while averaging 13:33 of ice time per game. This is the Scituate, Mass. native’s first full season in Columbus. He was traded to the Blue Jackets ahead of last year’s trade deadline from the Vancouver Canucks , as he was expected to provide an offensive boost as they battled to stay in the Wild Card race. He scored five goals and seven points in the remaining 21 games, but the Jackets came short of clinching a playoff berth. With Garland out, expect to see Ryan Lomberg back in the lineup, joining Steven Lorentz and Jack Williams on the fourth line during practice on Monday. The Blue Jackets (7-8-0) sit sixth in the Metropolitan Division, six points back of the last Wild Card position in the Eastern Conference.

The latest is a staple from the Capitals’ 2018 Stanley Cup championship run. Monday morning, on Spencer Carbery’s 45th birthday, Capitals players made the Jack Adams Trophy-winning coach do a “Hot Lap” [ Editor’s note: It is capitalized because it is Important.] Carbery’s pupils then tapped their sticks, singing Happy Birthday as he made his way around the MedStar Capitals Iceplex rink. items.body: A key member of the Toronto Maple Leafs ' future is currently sidelined. Top defence prospect Ben Danford has a broken wrist and is considered week-to-week, Toronto Marlies head coach Steve Sullivan told reporters. Danford suffered the broken wrist during a Nov. 4 win over the Hamilton Hammers when he blocked a pass. The 20-year-old is in his first full AHL season, after joining the Marlies for the 2026 playoffs en route to a Calder Cup. He finished his OHL career last season, after four years split between the Oshawa Generals and Brantford Bulldogs. Danford totalled 99 points in 233 OHL regular-season games and 19 points in 60 playoff contests. The Maple Leafs' No. 31 overall pick in the 2024 NHL Draft had a goal and two assists during the Marlies' playoff run last year, but has taken on a much bigger role this year. Instead, the United States pulled through with a 3-0 shutout win over Czechia, while Canada Red beat their national counterparts in the bronze medal game. While Schultz received the most hype, Madden Daneault is the one many expect to go first overall in 2029. We are now 41 days into the fantasy season and are witnessing teams start to separate in our league standings. It’s a long season, but we are nearing the quarter-mark. It was in the ninth minute of the second period when Xhekaj set up a great one-timer opportunity in the offensive zone for Adam Engstrom and then hustled back into position in his own end to simultaneously deny a zone entry and a hit from Viggo Bjorck. In both instances, Xhekaj steadied himself, chose the play he was going to make before the puck arrived, and executed to perfection. The pass to Engstrom was the best of several decisions Xhekaj could’ve made in that situation, and it led to a quality scoring chance. And everything he did immediately after that led to the Canadiens continuing one of their only good sequences of the game — and led Bjorck back to the Jets’ bench worse for wear after bearing the brunt of a collision he initiated. That had to feel good for Xhekaj, who was one of roughly five Canadiens who didn’t need a hard look in the mirror after that history-making loss. items.title: Ducks’ Cutter Gauthier becomes first NHLer with three hat-tricks in a 10-day span to start a month
items.summary: The Swedish-born American set unique history and ranks third in the NHL with 15 goals through 17 games.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Anaheim Ducks forward Cutter Gauthier is enjoying himself this season and making history as the Ducks establish themselves as one of the NHL’s most thrilling teams through the first quarter of the 2026-27 regular season. On Sunday night, with a three-goal, one-assist performance in a 5-2 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins , he became the first player in NHL history to score three hat tricks within the first 10 days of a calendar month. Gauthier leaned on an empty-net goal in the final minute to earn himself the historic honor, as the Ducks became the first team since the 1988-90 LA Kings to score at least five goals in eight consecutive games. The 22-year-old started the month in peak form, scoring his first November hat trick on Nov. 1 in a 6-3 win over the Ottawa Senators . Two days later, he potted another trio against the struggling Vancouver Canucks in a 5-4 victory. Both of his first two hat-tricks in November included two power-play goals, as he makes the most of Anaheim’s league-leading 38.5 percent success rate on the man advantage this season. Yet, his history-making performance against the Penguins didn’t need any special-teams help, with two goals coming at five-on-five before he netted the empty-net marker to seal the victory. Through 17 games this season, the Swedish-born American has 15 goals, good for third in the NHL, and seven assists for 22 points, ranking him 17th in NHL scoring overall. In his career, he has 76 goals and 60 assists for 136 points in 176 games with the Ducks and, previously, the Philadelphia Flyers . After Sunday’s win, the Ducks sit third in the Pacific Division with 21 points through the first 18 games of the 84-game campaign, as they look ahead to a Wednesday night home game against the Nashville Predators.

items.body: Mark Scheifele scored with 1.6 seconds remaining in the third period to lead the Winnipeg Jets to a 4-3 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning on Sunday. With the period winding down and the Jets on a 5-on-3 power play, Scheifele converted a pass from Cole Perfetti before firing home a slapshot to seal the win at Canada Life Centre. "(Perfetti) and Gabe (Vilardi) getting dirty in the corner and making a great play," Scheifele said of his goal after the win. items.body: Register Login Panthers Recall Jack Devine By Brian La Rose | at November 8, 2026 6:46 pm Prior to their game against Boston this afternoon, the Panthers added some extra depth to their forward group. The team announced that they’ve recalled winger Jack Devine from AHL Charlotte. The 23-year-old was a seventh-round pick back in 2021, going 221st overall in 2022 and has clearly outperformed that draft selection. After a strong four seasons at the University of Denver (including tallying 56 and 57 points in his final two years), Devine turned pro last season, playing predominantly with the Checkers. In 63 games with them in 2025-26, Devine had a good rookie campaign, tallying 18 goals and 25 assists. He had a brief two-week stint with Florida early on in the year, getting into six games with the Panthers although he was held off the scoresheet. This season, Devine got off to an impressive start with Charlotte, notching nine goals and three assists through 11 appearances. Devine’s recall comes on the heels of the injury that Sandis Vilmanis sustained on Saturday. Head coach Paul Maurice indicated that while they’ve had a doctor look at the youngster already, they probably won’t get a full assessment of the injury until they return home. Florida has one game left on its road trip on Tuesday in Columbus so it will be a few more days before the severity of the injury to Vilmanis is known. In the short term, Devine will serve as the extra forward while they get a better sense of how long Vilmanis will be out for. Depending on the severity of the injury, Florida could reassess who they want in the reserve role from there. Kicking off Year 12 for the undrafted veteran, Gourde is back on the second line alongside Anthony Cirelli and Brandon Hagel . The 34-year-old underwent hip surgery over the summer, and back in September it was thought he’d be out until December, returning considerably sooner than expected. Going from an ECHLer to a two-time Stanley Cup champion and legitimate top-six threat, Gourde returned to Tampa after 3 1/2 years with the Kraken. A beloved veteran no longer expected to drive the same amount of offense, he suited up for all 82 games last year recording 28 points. It was the fourth time the spark plug surpassed the 100-hit mark, landing 115. Facing multiple first round playoff exits, the Lightning made an effort to strengthen their middle-six along with adding a star in John Carlson . Their current 11-3-2 record speaks to the improvements made during the offseason. During Gourde’s absence the sudden uncertainty surrounding Nikita Kucherov dropped out of nowhere, but with whatever is in store with that situation, for now the Bolts boast one of the strongest top-nine forward groups in the league.

items.title: Report: Blackhawks not making coaching change amid slump
items.body: It appears the Chicago Blackhawks are staying the course amid some choppy waters. Jeff Blashill will remain as Blackhawks' head coach as the team has opted not to make a coaching change, The Athletic 's Scott Powers reported on Sunday. The Blackhawks, in a rebuild for the better part of a decade, were intending this to be a season in which they turned a corner. Instead, they've started the year 4-13-1 — better only than the lowly Vancouver Canucks in the Western Conference. Things hit a low point with a 9-2 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes on Saturday night. The Blackhawks were off Sunday and don't play again until Thursday, which led many to wonder whether regime change is imminent. Instead, it appears general manager Kyle Davidson is giving Blashill some more time to right the ship. The former Detroit Red Wings coach was hired by Chicago ahead of the 2025-26 season. The Blackhawks missed the playoffs for the sixth consecutive season with a 29-39-14 record.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images A couple of netminders have hit the wire. On Sunday, the Chicago Blackhawks placed goaltender Arvid Soderblom on waivers, with the Washington Capitals doing the same with fellow backstop Remi Poirier. Soderblom entered the 2026-27 season set to be the backup to Spencer Knight once again. However, while the Blackhawks have struggled as a whole, Soderblom’s play has been anything but up to par. In five appearances so far, four starts, the 27-year-old has allowed 21 goals, giving him a 4.67 goals-against average and a .842 save percentage, along with a 0-3-1 record. Who the Hawks would call up to take his place is yet to be determined. Drew Commesso has been with the organization the longest, having played a couple of games with Chicago on top of his time with the AHL’s Rockford IceHogs, but Stanislav Berezhnoy has had better numbers early on this year with Rockford. In 117 NHL games, Soderblom has a record of 25-68-15, with a 3.65 GAA, a .885 SV% and one shutout. He’s in the final season of his two-year contract extension, which he signed in July 2025. The deal carries an AAV of $2.75 million. Poirier was acquired by the Capitals last Sunday in exchange for a seventh-round pick from the New Jersey Devils , as the Devils had to make some roster moves after receiving Connor Hellebuyck from the Winnipeg Jets . Poirier, who was claimed off waivers by the Devils from the Dallas Stars , has yet to play a game this season. He has spent the past three seasons with the Stars’ top farm team, the Texas Stars. In 137 regular-season games in the AHL, the 25-year-old is 70-51-16, with a 2.76 GAA, a .908 SV% and six shutouts. He’s also 11-9 in 23 Calder Cup Playoff contests, with a 2.42 GAA, a .909 SV% and three shutouts.
